name: UmlautAdaptarrEX
description: UmlautAdaptarrEX - Umlaut and multi-language title proxy for Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr and Prowlarr. Complete Next.js + Fastify + Prisma rewrite of the legacy .NET UmlautAdaptarr. Sits between your *Arr stack and the indexers, rewrites searches and Newznab/Torznab responses on the fly so releases with umlauts, German titles, TVDB aliases or bad naming are reliably found, downloaded and imported. Ships a full Web UI with setup wizard, dashboard, library browser, sync runs, request and rename history, and live WebSocket logs. Configuration and title cache are stored in a persistent SQLite DB under /data - no external database required. Highlights: Sonarr / Radarr (native via alternateTitles + optional TMDB) / Lidarr / Readarr / Prowlarr / NZB Hydra support, multiple instances per *Arr type, language plugins (German umlauts, Swedish umlauts, French accents) that can be combined, configurable title providers (TVDB, TMDB, db-cache), configurable search fan-out and release renaming, manual title overrides, two operating modes (Prowlarr indexer proxy on 5006 or direct as indexer on 5005), optional headless mode without the Web UI, UI in German, English, Swedish and French. Ports: 5007 Web UI (open http:// :5007/setup after the first start), 5005 Fastify API - the URL your *Arrs point at, 5006 HTTP-CONNECT proxy for Prowlarr indexers. IMPORTANT - 1:1 port mapping: each port variable sets both the in-container bind port and the published host port, so host and container side must always be identical. To move a service to another port, change the host port, the container port AND the matching UMLAUTADAPTARREX_*_PORT variable to the same value. A mismatched mapping breaks /api proxying and the indexer URLs your *Arrs point at.

paths.name: App Data
paths.description: Persistent storage for the SQLite database (umlautadaptarrex.db) and the title-cache. Do NOT delete - it contains all your *Arr connections, API keys and matching state. Ownership is fixed automatically on container start (see PUID/PGID).

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: HTTP port for the Next.js web UI. Open this in your browser to reach the setup wizard and admin panel. IMPORTANT: the host port and the container port MUST be identical (1:1 mapping). To use a non-default port, change this value AND set the matching UMLAUTADAPTARREX_WEBUI_PORT variable below to the SAME number.

ports.name: API Port
ports.description: Fastify API + WebSocket port. This is the URL you point your *Arr instances at (e.g. http://unraid-ip:5005/apikey/sonarr/api). Also serves /api/admin, /api/auth, /titlelookup and /ws/logs. IMPORTANT: the host port and the container port MUST be identical (1:1 mapping). To use a non-default port, change this value AND set the matching UMLAUTADAPTARREX_LEGACYAPI_PORT variable below to the SAME number.

ports.name: Indexer Proxy Port
ports.description: TCP HTTP-CONNECT proxy for Prowlarr indexers. Configure this as Prowlarr's HTTP proxy so indexer responses get rewritten on the fly. IMPORTANT: the host port and the container port MUST be identical (1:1 mapping). To use a non-default port, change this value AND set the matching UMLAUTADAPTARREX_PROXY_PORT variable below to the SAME number.

variables.name: API Port (variable)
variables.description: In-container bind port for the Fastify API. MUST match the 'API Port' mapping above (1:1: host port = container port = this value). The image reads ONLY this branded variable -- the legacy PORT fallback was removed in 1.2.2. Leave at 5005 unless you also remapped the 'API Port' above to the same number.

variables.name: Web UI Port (variable)
variables.description: In-container bind port for the Next.js Web UI. MUST match the 'Web UI Port' mapping above (1:1: host port = container port = this value). The image reads ONLY this branded variable -- the legacy WEB_PORT fallback was removed in 1.2.2. Leave at 5007 unless you also remapped the 'Web UI Port' above to the same number.

variables.name: Indexer Proxy Port (variable)
variables.description: In-container bind port for the Prowlarr HTTP-CONNECT proxy. MUST match the 'Indexer Proxy Port' mapping above (1:1: host port = container port = this value). When set, it overrides the value stored in the database on every start and the Settings UI shows the proxy port read-only. Leave at 5006 unless you also remapped the 'Indexer Proxy Port' above to the same number.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: UID the app runs as. Default 99 = Unraid `nobody`, which matches the rest of your appdata shares. The entrypoint chowns /data to PUID:PGID on every start.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: GID the app runs as. Default 100 = Unraid `users` group.

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Berlin, UTC, America/New_York). Affects timestamps in logs and the Web UI.

variables.name: LOG_LEVEL
variables.description: Pino log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal.

variables.name: TRUST_PROXY
variables.description: Only needed behind an EXTERNAL reverse proxy (Traefik / NPM / Caddy on another host or in another container). Controls how far X-Forwarded-* headers are trusted. Default 'loopback' trusts them only for requests arriving via 127.0.0.1/::1. Use a comma-separated list of trusted CIDRs/IPs for an external proxy, or 'true' to trust any hop. Hop counts (e.g. '1') are NOT supported and are ignored with a startup warning. Leave empty to keep the default.

variables.name: Headless Mode (no Web UI)
variables.description: Optional. Set to 1 to run WITHOUT the Next.js Web UI (and without the self-forking supervisor) as a single process, saving roughly a third / ~50-90 MB RAM. ONLY for an already-configured instance: complete the setup wizard once with the Web UI first, then set this to 1. On an unconfigured database the container refuses to start with an explanatory message. When enabled you can remove the 'Web UI Port' mapping (5007). Leave empty to keep the Web UI (default).
